% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
% Section 5 (Mitigation) -- training and analysis as run
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
We train QLoRA-DPO adapters (4-bit NF4 base, LoRA rank 16 on all attention and MLP projections, $\beta=0.1$, learning rate $5\times10^{-5}$, effective batch 16, fp16 on T4 GPUs) on equal pair budgets per model: 39 for Phi-3-mini and 60 for Llama-3.2, the number of reviewed CS pairs available for Phi-3 and the planned cap for Llama. B uses PKU-SafeRLHF pairs with exactly one safe response; C uses the model's own reviewed CS failures paired with written refusals. B and C are each trained with three seeds. A learning check declared before training required a final-epoch DPO loss $\le 0.60$ and reward accuracy $\ge 0.75$ on the seed-42 B and C adapters of both models; it failed at 2 epochs and passed at 4, which all adapters then used (Table~\ref{tab:p2-training}).
\verify{Disclose: fp16 loss scaling skipped the first 2--4 optimizer steps of every adapter (gradient overflow while the scale calibrates), so the main adapters received 5--9 effective updates; the 2-epoch failure is largely this. Adapters B\_ext\_phi3\_n30\_ablation\_D6, C\_llama32\_n25, C\_phi3\_n25, C\_phi3\_n30\_ablation\_D6 received 0--2 effective updates and fail the same check: their results are reported as not trained. The first full run stalled after the learning check; the reported run repeated it on three Kaggle accounts with the same code, versions and 4 epochs, and re-recorded the check with the same outcome.}

Before any Phase-2 output was judged we fixed the analysis: for each family, C's and B's outcomes are the mean judge label over the three seeds; the primary test is a two-sided paired sign-flip permutation test over families, Holm-adjusted across the two models, and a contrast is a finding only if it is Holm-significant and its judge-corrected interval excludes zero with the same sign. Judge error is corrected with the Phase-1 predictive values of that model and condition unless a blinded audit of post-training responses shows that they changed; the audit (300 responses, Table~\ref{tab:p2-audit}) changed none.
\verify{Disclose: the audit's switch rule was reworded the same day, before any output was judged (from ``outside the Phase-1 interval'' to a Fisher exact test).}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
% Section 6 -- Mitigation results
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
For Llama-3.2, training on its own CS failures reduces CS harmful compliance more than the same number of external English pairs: $-$9.7 points raw, $-$6.8 after judge correction (95\% interval [$-$11.3, $-$2.6], Holm $p$ = .004; Table~\ref{tab:rq4}), with the same sign in every seed. For Phi-3-mini neither recipe moves harmful compliance (+0.3 points, $p$ = .903): its CS rate is already near its floor, and most of its Roman-Urdu and Urdu-script responses are non-responses in every arm (Figure~\ref{fig:p2-composition}). The Phi-3 result is limited evidence, not evidence of equal effectiveness.

C lowers Llama's harmful compliance mainly by refusing more often, not by producing broken output (Figure~\ref{fig:p2-composition}); it transfers to Roman Urdu but not to Urdu script, and slightly lowers English harmful compliance (Figure~\ref{fig:p2-effects}). Neither recipe increases refusal of harmless prompts, and capability is retained (Table~\ref{tab:mitigation}). The safety system prompt (E) gives the largest reductions but makes both models refuse many harmless prompts, most of all in Roman Urdu. Withholding the D6 domain from training leaves Llama's CS reduction on D6 similar in size, with intervals too wide to separate the two (Table~\ref{tab:p2-ncurve}).
A blinded review of 64 responses that C still produced and the judge flagged (Table~\ref{tab:p2-residual}) confirms nearly all English and most CS flags; the confirmed harmful responses mostly comply directly or after a warning or a fictional or educational frame, and none arise from misreading the request.
\verify{After training, only 4/16 RU and 6/16 UR judge-flagged C responses were confirmed harmful (Table~\ref{tab:p2-residual}), while RU/UR corrections use Phase-1 error rates that were not re-audited after training and only C's flagged responses were reviewed (no unflagged sample, no A): treat the RU/UR transfer estimates as uncertain and say so in Limitations.}
\verify{Phi-3 UrduMMLU is near chance (0.27) in every arm; Llama C UrduMMLU retention 0.949 (6 of 300 items). The judge's precision on flagged Phi-3 CS responses was 23/30 in the audit vs 14/14 in Phase 1 (not significant; Exp~6 review 44/66) -- state as a caveat.}
